svg.aria-label: Embedding map: each dot is a sentence about my work, embedded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and projected with PCA.

circle.title: YT Lecture RAG searches 126 YouTube DSA lectures and jumps to the second where a topic is explained.
Lecture transcripts are chunked into 75-second windows with 15 seconds of overlap.
The lecture index holds 2,933 transcript chunks from about 68 hours of video.
Transcript chunks are embedded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and stored in a local Qdrant collection.
A distance cutoff drops retrieved chunks that are too far from the query.
A title-word boost ranks a lecture higher when the query matches its title.
A small Groq model rewrites Hinglish questions into English DSA search queries.
Rewritten search queries are cached so a repeated question skips the LLM call.
Ask a DSA question in Hinglish or English and land on the exact lecture timestamp.
The English-only embedder matched Hinglish queries by language instead of by topic.
Query rewriting fixed the mismatch between Hinglish questions and English transcripts.
Embeddings run through fastembed with ONNX so lecture search fits on Vercel.
Vector search over transcript chunks returns the top five candidate moments.
Grounded answers are generated only from retrieved lecture excerpts.
Each grounded answer has to cite the lecture excerpt it draws from.
The retrieval eval uses a golden set of 20 questions plus 8 off-topic questions.
Query rewriting raised hit@5 from 65% to 95%.
Mean reciprocal rank rose from about 0.59 to 0.77 after query rewriting.
Top-1 accuracy went from about 55% to 65% with query rewriting.
All 8 off-topic questions in the golden set are refused.
Moving to fastembed ONNX left hit@5, top-1 and MRR unchanged.
Retrieval quality is measured with hit@k and MRR at k = 5.
The answer is refused when nothing survives the distance cutoff.
The answer is refused when the model says the excerpts don't cover the question.
The answer is refused when it has no valid citation.
Every setup is scored against the baseline on the same golden set.
HireMeAI says it is not in the resume instead of inventing an answer.
HireMeAI is a recruiter chatbot that answers only from my resume.
The resume is parsed once into a strict JSON schema.
The parsed resume is committed as a cache keyed on file, prompt and model.
Production startup makes zero LLM calls because the parsed resume is cached.
HireMeAI streams its replies and keeps a 10-message chat window.
HireMeAI calls Groq with the openai/gpt-oss-120b model.
Pydantic models enforce the structured output schema.
gpt-oss reasoning tokens count toward the output limit, which cut off long structured outputs.
Groq returned 400 json_validate_failed instead of a length finish reason when output was cut off.
Setting max_completion_tokens explicitly fixed the truncated structured outputs.
My phone number is withheld from the model.
HireMeAI has defenses against prompt injection and XSS.
The HireMeAI frontend is built with React and Vite.
MealTime generates recipes with Gemini and falls back to Groq.
MealTime can remix a recipe with AI.
MealTime plans meals across several days with AI.
FastAPI serves the Python backends for YT Lecture RAG and HireMeAI.
I work with the Groq and Gemini APIs.
MealTime is an AI recipe and meal-planning Android app.
MealTime is written in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose.
MealTime follows MVVM with Clean Architecture.
Hilt handles dependency injection in MealTime.
A 5-table Room cache keeps MealTime recipes available offline.
MealTime ships a bundled offline fallback for recipes.
MealTime has recipe search, a cooking mode and favorites.
The MealTime shopping list is grouped by recipe.
MealTime subscriptions use Play Billing 7.
Firebase Auth, Firestore and Crashlytics back the MealTime app.
Kometo is a food-delivery app built with Jetpack Compose.
Kometo uses Clean Architecture, Hilt and Firebase Auth.
MyWishlist is an offline wishlist manager built on Room.
MyWishlist uses Kotlin Flow with MVVM.
I build Android apps with Coroutines, Flow and Retrofit.
MealTime's AI requests go through a Cloudflare Worker, so no API keys ship in the APK.
The Cloudflare Worker authenticates each request with a Firebase ID token.
Subscriptions are enforced server-side by validating Play purchase tokens.
A validated purchase sets a Firebase custom claim on the user.
YT Lecture RAG is deployed on Vercel.
HireMeAI runs on free hosting on Render, so the first load can take a minute.
HireMeAI enforces per-IP and global rate limits.
Only valid requests count against the HireMeAI rate limits.
Per-IP limits can be spoofed via X-Forwarded-For; the global cap bounds the damage.
The DSA tracker syncs progress across devices through Supabase.
Supabase row-level security protects each user's synced progress.
I work with AWS Lambda, API Gateway, SQS and DynamoDB.
I provision cloud infrastructure with Terraform.
I have worked with AWS EC2 and VPC networking.
AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer – Associate, earned in April 2026.
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate, earned in April 2026.
AWS Certified AI Practitioner, earned in December 2025.
AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner, earned in December 2025.
HireMeAI has 31 pytest tests with the LLM mocked.
The HireMeAI test suite runs in about two seconds.
Mocking the LLM lets the HireMeAI tests run without calling the API.
The DSA tracker is covered by Vitest unit tests.
Playwright end-to-end tests cover the DSA tracker.
MealTime CI runs unit tests on every push.
GitHub Actions builds and lints MealTime on every push.
I write tests with pytest, Vitest and Playwright.
The DSA Practice Tracker holds 917 problems across 23 topics.
Problems come back for review at 7, 30 and 90 days.
A failed review drops a problem to a 3-day re-check.
The DSA tracker is an installable, offline-first PWA.
Cross-device sync is optional and uses Google sign-in.
Progress from different devices is merged when it syncs.
The DSA tracker is built with React, Vite and Tailwind.
YT Lecture RAG finds where a DSA topic is explained across 68 hours of lectures.
I have solved 450+ LeetCode problems.
I kept a LeetCode streak of more than 100 days.
I practice data structures and algorithms in C++.
I was a national-level participant in the Bharatiya Antariksh Hackathon 2025.
